name: viva-biofilm-capabilities
title: viva-biofilm capabilities: spatial structure, performance, and composability
biological_story:
A biofilm begins as a handful of cells attached to a surface. As they grow
and divide, they consume the solutes diffusing in from the bulk liquid
faster than diffusion can replenish them near the substratum, so a
concentration gradient forms: richer at the boundary, poorer at the base.
That gradient in turn shapes where growth is fastest, producing the
characteristic spatially structured, substrate-limited colony this
investigation demonstrates and visualizes.
question:
Beyond well-mixed equivalence to the reference model (the viva-biofilm-equivalence
investigation), what does the viva-biofilm Rust + process-bigraph engine
make possible that the Java tool does not: fast, deterministic spatial
biofilm simulation with beautiful interactive visuals, measured performance
scaling, and composability with external control processes?

executive.what_is_this:
A demonstration investigation for the viva-biofilm engine's viva-native
capabilities: a spatially developed biofilm (colony structure, solute
gradients, growth curves) rendered as interactive Plotly figures, its
runtime/scaling characteristics, and its composability with a boundary
controller process — all built on the Phase-A Rust core (BiofilmProcess)
now ~23x faster and deterministic after unit reconciliation and
calibration.

scientific_argument.main_claim:
viva-biofilm grows a spatially structured, substrate-limited biofilm from
a small inoculum using fixed (non-tuned) parameters, in seconds, with
reproducible (seeded) determinism — and this spatial capability composes
with process-bigraph the same way the well-mixed chemostat path does.
evidence_for: spatial-biofilm-growth: 40 -> 640 agents, 12.1 um thickness, substratum/boundary substrate ratio 0.49 (a clear substrate-limitation gradient), from one fixed, deterministic run (this study).
runtime-and-scaling: ~303,000 agent-steps/sec peak throughput; grid, population, and duration scaling curves all produced with no configuration exceeding the 30s slow threshold (this study).

composability: a BoundaryControllerProcess drove the oxygen boundary on schedule (0.5 g/m^3 during t=1d-3d, restored to 8.74 after, matching reference exactly) and the biofilm's growth visibly responded -- 60 vs. 120 final agents, biomass ratio 0.574 vs. an identically-seeded un-perturbed control (this study).
caveats: IbM is stochastic; results are single-seed demonstrations of qualitative behavior, not statistical ensembles.
PDE/relaxation/detachment are simplified vs iDynoMiCS's exact algorithms (see viva-biofilm-equivalence for the well-mixed quantitative equivalence claim).
Duration scaling is near- but not exactly linear (R^2=0.907): population growth via division during longer runs compounds per-step cost.

studies.name: spatial-biofilm-growth
studies.title: Spatial biofilm growth: a developed colony with a real substrate gradient
studies.question:
Starting from a small inoculum of 40 agents, does the viva-biofilm spatial
engine grow a visibly developed 2D biofilm — hundreds of agents, a
measurable thickness above the substratum, and a genuine substrate-limitation
gradient (boundary richer than substratum) — within a short, deterministic,
non-swept run?

studies.name: runtime-and-scaling
studies.title: Runtime and scaling: throughput and scaling curves for the Rust engine
studies.question:
After the ~23x performance pass and the addition of configurable PDE
parameters, how does the viva-biofilm engine's wall-time scale with grid
size, agent population, and run duration -- and what throughput
(agent-steps/sec) does it sustain?

studies.name: composability
studies.title: Composability: a boundary controller process perturbing the biofilm at runtime
studies.question:
Does viva-biofilm's boundary_concentrations runtime hook (the Task 6
set_bulk_by_name binding) actually compose with an external
process-bigraph control process -- can a BoundaryControllerProcess drive
the biofilm's oxygen boundary on a schedule and produce a visible,
measurable growth response, the same way process-bigraph composes any two
processes sharing a store?
